description: Public UI improvements: items 1–10 and 18. These all touch public-facing components and pages. They are independent of the admin changes in FEAT-003 and can be done in any order relative to it, but must come after FEAT-001 (dark mode removal) to avoid reintroducing dark: classes. Covers: hero section redesign with animated paper count (#1), PaperCard hover tooltip + trending badge + prefetch (#2, #10, #18), PaperList empty state + skeleton (#4, #5), paper detail page breadcrumb + print/copy/share buttons + related papers (#3, #7, #8), recently viewed component (#9), sticky search bar (#6).
steps:
STEP 1 — Item #1: Redesign hero in src/app/(public)/page.tsx. The page is a Server Component. Add a counter query: `const { count: paperCount } = await supabase.from('papers').select('*', { count: 'exact', head: true }).eq('status', 'published')`. Pass `paperCount` to the hero section. In the hero JSX, add below the subtitle

: `

{(paperCount ?? 0).toLocaleString()}+ past papers available

`. The TTU logo + content split layout already exists (flex flex-col sm:flex-row) — keep it, just add the counter. The search bar already appears inside the hero — keep it.

STEP 2 — Item #2: Add CSS-only hover tooltip to PaperCard in src/components/PaperCard.tsx. The article already has `group` class. Add a tooltip div just before the closing : `

{course?.name ?? ''}

{course?.programme ?? ''}

`. Use `md:hidden md:group-hover:block` approach: add `hidden group-hover:block md:hidden md:group-hover:block` — but simpler and CSS-only: use opacity trick with `opacity-0 pointer-events-none group-hover:opacity-100 group-hover:pointer-events-auto` so it never shifts layout. Final: `className='absolute inset-x-0 top-full z-20 mt-1 rounded-lg bg-white px-3 py-2 shadow-lg ring-1 ring-gray-200 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity duration-150 pointer-events-none'`. Only show on md+ by wrapping with `hidden md:block` parent. The article must have `overflow-visible` — remove any overflow-hidden if present (there is none). Ensure article has `position: relative` — it already has `relative` in className.

STEP 3 — Item #10: Add trending badge to PaperCard in src/components/PaperCard.tsx. In the card's top-left area, after the top color bar div and before the p-4 content div, add: `{(paper.downloads ?? 0) > 10 && (🔥 Trending)}`. The article already has `relative` class so absolute positioning works.
STEP 4 — Item #18: Confirm/add explicit prefetch to PaperCard Link. In src/components/PaperCard.tsx, the existing `<Link href={'/papers/'+paper.id} ...>` — add `prefetch={true}` prop explicitly.

STEP 5 — Item #5: Improve loading skeleton in src/components/PaperList.tsx. Replace the existing SkeletonCard function body with a shape matching the real PaperCard: colored top bar (h-1 bg-gray-200 rounded-t-2xl), then a p-4 div containing: row of two badge placeholders (h-5 w-16 and h-5 w-12 rounded-full bg-gray-200), course code placeholder (h-3 w-1/4 rounded bg-gray-200 mt-3), two title lines (h-4 w-full and h-4 w-3/4 rounded bg-gray-200), semester badge placeholder (h-5 w-16 rounded-full bg-gray-200 mt-3), footer row with download icon and view button placeholder.

STEP 6 — Item #4: Enhance empty state in src/components/PaperList.tsx. Replace the existing simple magnifying-glass SVG with a more illustrative inline SVG (books + magnifying glass, brand-colored). The existing empty state already has the correct message text ('No papers found.' and 'Try adjusting your search or filters.') — keep those. Replace the SVG with a larger 80x80 books illustration: draw a simple open book with a magnifying glass in brand-primary color (#1d4ed8). Use `fill='none' stroke='#1d4ed8' strokeWidth='1.5'` on the SVG element with `width='80' height='80' viewBox='0 0 24 24'`. Book path: `<path d='M2 3h6a4 4 0 0 1 4 4v14a3 3 0 0 0-3-3H2z'/><path d='M22 3h-6a4 4 0 0 0-4 4v14a3 3 0 0 1 3-3h7z'/>`. Magnifying glass (smaller, offset): `<circle cx='18' cy='5' r='2'/><line x1='19.5' y1='6.5' x2='21' y2='8'/>`. Wrap entire empty state in a py-20 centered div.

STEP 7 — Item #3: Breadcrumb on paper detail page. Already implemented in src/app/(public)/papers/[id]/page.tsx (uses nav + ol + aria-label='Breadcrumb' with / separators). The task asks for › separators. Change the two `
  • /
    • ` separators to `›` character. Also truncate the title in the last breadcrumb item to 40 chars: `{paper.title.length > 40 ? paper.title.slice(0, 40) + '…' : paper.title}`. The existing breadcrumb already has `max-w-[200px] truncate` on the last item but the task wants explicit 40-char truncation.

STEP 8 — Item #7: Print and Copy link buttons on paper detail page (src/app/(public)/papers/[id]/page.tsx). The existing page is a Server Component. Create a new client component file src/app/(public)/papers/[id]/ActionButtons.tsx. It exports `function ActionButtons()`. It has two buttons: 1) 'Copy link' — onClick calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(window.location.href)` then sets a `copied` state to true for 2s via setTimeout. When copied=true, shows 'Copied!' text. 2) 'Print' — onClick calls `window.print()`. Style both as: `rounded-md border border-gray-300 px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-50 transition-colors`. In the paper detail page.tsx, import ActionButtons and render it after the DownloadButton inside the card div.

STEP 9 — Item #8: Related papers section on paper detail page. In src/app/(public)/papers/[id]/page.tsx (Server Component), after fetching the main paper, add a related papers query: `const { data: relatedPapers } = await supabase.from('papers').select<'*, courses(*)', PaperWithCourse>('*, courses(*)').eq('status', 'published').eq('course_id', paper.course_id).neq('id', paper.id).order('created_at', { ascending: false }).limit(4)`. Below the main card div, add a section: `{relatedPapers && relatedPapers.length > 0 && (

More from {course?.code ?? 'this course'}

{relatedPapers.map(p => )}
)}`. Import PaperCard from '@/components/PaperCard'.

STEP 10 — Item #9: Recently viewed papers. Create new client component src/components/RecentlyViewed.tsx. It accepts `{ papers: PaperWithCoursePublic[] }` as props. If papers array is empty, renders nothing. Otherwise renders: `

Recently viewed

{papers.map(p => )}
`. Import PaperCard and PaperWithCoursePublic from '@/components/PaperCard'. Mark with 'use client'. In src/app/(public)/page.tsx (Server Component), do NOT read localStorage (server can't). Instead, pass the recently-viewed IDs via a client-side approach: create a wrapper client component src/components/RecentlyViewedWrapper.tsx marked 'use client' that on mount reads `localStorage.getItem('pq:recentlyViewed')`, parses the JSON array of IDs (up to 5), fetches `/api/papers?ids=...` — but since the API doesn't support ids filter, use a simpler approach: fetch each paper individually from `/api/papers/[id]` in parallel. Once resolved, render ``. In src/app/(public)/page.tsx, add `` above the FilterPanel section. In src/app/(public)/papers/[id]/page.tsx, add a client component src/app/(public)/papers/[id]/SaveToHistory.tsx marked 'use client' that in useEffect on mount does: `const stored = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('pq:recentlyViewed') ?? '[]'); const updated = [paperId, ...stored.filter((id: string) => id !== paperId)].slice(0, 5); localStorage.setItem('pq:recentlyViewed', JSON.stringify(updated))`. It renders nothing (returns null). Import and render `` at the top of the paper detail page content.

STEP 11 — Item #6: Sticky search bar. Create src/components/StickySearch.tsx as a client component ('use client'). It accepts `{ heroRef: React.RefObject }` as props — but since we're in a Server Component page, use a different approach: create a client component src/components/StickySearchWrapper.tsx that renders a hero sentinel div and uses IntersectionObserver to show/hide a compact sticky bar. The sticky bar floats at top-0 z-40 fixed. When visible it shows just the SearchBar. Implementation: the wrapper renders a `
` placed just after the hero section, observes it with IntersectionObserver({ threshold: 0 }). When sentinel leaves viewport (isHeroVisible = false), show the sticky bar. The sticky bar: `
`. The hero section already has the public layout's sticky header at top-0 z-30. The sticky search goes at z-40 so it appears over content but below modals. In src/app/(public)/page.tsx, import and render `` as a Suspense-wrapped client import (use dynamicImport with ssr:false) placed just before the filters section.
acceptance_criteria: Home page hero shows a paper count like '42+ past papers available' (number comes from DB query).
Hovering a PaperCard on desktop (md+) shows a tooltip with course name and programme.
PaperCards with downloads > 10 show a 🔥 Trending badge in top-left.
Loading skeleton matches PaperCard shape with colored top bar.
Empty state shows brand-colored book SVG with correct message.
Paper detail breadcrumb uses › separators and truncates title to 40 chars.
Paper detail page has Copy link and Print buttons that work.
Paper detail page shows 'More from [course code]' section with up to 4 related papers.
RecentlyViewed wrapper component exists and renders on home page.
SaveToHistory component exists and saves paper ID to localStorage on paper detail page.
StickySearchWrapper exists and renders a fixed search bar that appears on scroll.
npm run build passes with zero errors.
findings: All 11 steps implemented. Hero paper count added via Supabase count query. PaperCard updated with hover tooltip (md+), 🔥 Trending badge (downloads > 10), and explicit prefetch={true}. PaperList skeleton redesigned to match card shape; empty state SVG replaced with brand-colored books illustration. Paper detail breadcrumb uses › separators with 40-char title truncation. ActionButtons.tsx (copy link + print) and SaveToHistory.tsx created and wired into paper detail page. Related papers section fetches up to 4 same-course papers. RecentlyViewed.tsx and RecentlyViewedWrapper.tsx created; wrapper dynamically imported (ssr:false) on home page. StickySearchWrapper.tsx created using IntersectionObserver; dynamically imported (ssr:false) on home page. One TypeScript fix needed: paper.course_id is string|null — guarded with if check before Supabase query. npm run build and npm run test:unit both pass.
